questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic program being relevant for my future plans in terms of what I couldn't get from UCPH as well as being close to my friends in London.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Once I got here it was relatively easy and there was a lot of guidance from the university but before I actually arrived it felt a bit chaotic as I didn't have it confirmed what accommodation I was gonna live in despite having applied for student accommodation until like 2 weeks before I got here as well as not being told which classes I could take and having to go back and forth between the exchange office because they wouldn't answer my emails about classes. I ended up not having my classes until the weekend right before classes actually started so that was a bit stressful to be honest. Once I had my classes however, it has been really interesting and teachers have been very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't need any assistance but I went to a couple of freshers events which there were lots of - both parties but also just non-alcoholic things you could do like planting a plant and decorating frames. Overall I liked how open people were that first week of freshers cuz it seemed like everybody were really keen on making friends and meeting new people which I think was probably fueled by the university having lots of events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Accommodation was really easy but as mentioned above actually getting my classes were a bit of a hassle.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different types of rooms through student accommodation

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I think you could pay for a meal plan and have food at your accommodation but I didn't have that. I've shared a kitchen with 6 other people in the halls I've stayed at and tbh my diet has been horrible here because the kitchen is disgusting and I haven't wanted to cook. There has been a cleaner every second week and then we switch amongst us who live here to clean every second week but even with that people have just not been great with cleaning after themselves when they've cooked so it's just always kinda gross in there and has made me not wan't to cook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you can squeeze it into your budget get a room with your own bathroom. I didn't and in our flat that we share as 7 people we have 2 bathrooms but in one of them the water doesn't get warm and despite making complaint after complaint about it it has not been fixed. The second bathroom is gross and theres barely any water that comes out if you want to shower in warm water so I've basically only showered at the gym. Also the beds are really bad, like you can feel the springs in the mattress. However, it is nice that if something isn't working (besides the shower evidently) you can make a complaint and someone usually comes to look at it the same day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was back and forth and back and forth with the registration office. I was told I had to enroll before a specific date but I never got the enrolement papers until like 2 days before the deadline. I had originally chosen this university because they had a course that would be really relevant to me, however, when I was enroling they told me they didnt have a partneship with UCPH for that specific program despite saying so on their website. So I was back and forth to figure out what i should do instead. In the end I finally got enrolled but in a different course than I had originally chosen the uni for and only like the day of the deadline because they hadn't sent me the form til enroll.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I talked to i think the exchange office who sometimes were quick to answer, sometimes not so quick.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Well as mentioned above I wanted to be on a completely different course but that wasn't available for exchange so I ended up being on somethign completely differetn. Although it has been really interesting its a shame that I couldnt get what I wanted in the beginning as it would filled out a crucial part of a subject that I would like to have more formal training in that I cant get from UCPH

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be large with what you can get. Don't be too specific about classes as you might not be able to get those exact ones.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have really enjoyed the academic part of my stay here despite it being different than what I expected when I applied for exchange.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All courses had to be MA level for UCPH to accept them. I found the actual classes sometimes didn't actually seem like MA level though because a lot of students don't have suficient english levels or don't have a background of (in my case) media studies to fully understand and have the tools to do something like analysis. I especially found it annoying that I felt like the fact that a lot of people didn't speak proper english took down the level of the class

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar - lots of seminars and discussion

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Stardom and celebrity culture
- Philosophy of sex, sexuality and gender
- Memory in National and Transnational Contexts
- Nation, Power, Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Philosophy of sex, sexuality and gender was really intersting and the english difficulties really wasn't an issue in that class and Nation, Power, Culture was really such an intersting class, however the exam felt a bit undergrad as we weren't allowed to choose what we wanted to write our essay about ourselves but were given specific questions we had to answer.

questions.answer: I spent a lot more money on eating out or buying meals than I used to in CPH because I didn't feel comfortbale cooking in our kitchen

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: You get a free buspass from the University if you live in student accommodation so transport was far less

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a great gym and swimming pool. I went to a couple of intros for different societies but found them all a bit too like undergrad for me unfortunately

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think if you can fidn a society you think fits you thats great!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around the country - I went to stonehenge and Bristol and a couple different things, and spent a lot of time in London

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: besides food, easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I was put into a mixed nationality flat and I think tbh that has been a part of the reason why the kitchen has been kinda gross because people come from such different backgrounds and have different attitudes to whom does what, and what boundaries are. And the fact that becuase my english is quite good i often felt like in the classes where the majority of the students don't speak english well i often felt like the teachers were kinda depending on us students who speaks english well to basically do all the talking in class while also teaching our fellowe students once we were put into group work. i didnt like that because i dint like the feeling of "being better" than my fellow students and sometimes i felt like they didn't want to say anything maybe because they were afraid of saying something wrong or because they didnt feel comfrotbale in english, which made me feel a bit like i was seen as like better than them or something which i really didnt like

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the unpretentiousness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: be open and go to some of the freshers events, if you need vegetables go to the nisa local on highfield campus and get the southern fried chicken salad, and get a gym membership to southampton sport if you dont like the showers at your accommodation

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No i think that pretty much sums it up

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Knowing I can do something as moving away and really enjoy it

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: figuring out how to do food in a country where the food culture is very different and where i didn't feel like i could cook that much

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
